overallVerdict: PMFREAK CRITICAL PATH PARTIAL — REMEDIATION BACKLOG READY

backlog.title: Legacy onboarding wizard fabricates data and bypasses evidence-derived activation
evidence: tests/workspace-onboarding-guardrails.test.mjs:4,46 (guardrail scans only the new surface, not this file)
backlog.currentBehavior: New users are routed to /workspace/setup, which renders GettingStartedFlow — a pre-#547 wizard that computes fabricated readiness/completion scores from arithmetic on string lengths, ships hardcoded fake evidence templates that get persisted as real operational_memory rows unless the user edits every field, includes a demo-data seeding branch with a fictional project, and writes a static onboarding_completed boolean.
backlog.expectedBehavior: The only onboarding surface a new user encounters is the evidence-derived activation engine from PR #547 (src/lib/workspace-activation/*), computing state purely from real workspace/project/task/signal presence, with no fabricated scores, no persisted fake evidence, and no demo-seeding branch.
backlog.rootCauseHypothesis: PR #547 built a new, correct activation engine but never retired the pre-existing wizard or rerouted the onboarding entry point to it; the guardrail regression test added by #547 only covers the new surface, so the legacy wizard's fabrication was never caught by CI.
backlog.implementationBoundary: Retire or fully rewrite getting-started-flow.tsx and its API route to use only real, evidence-derived data; reroute /workspace/setup (or retire it) so the canonical entry point is the #547 activation engine.
nonGoals: Do not redesign the activation engine's underlying evidence rules (activation-rules.ts) — those are already correct.
Do not rebuild onboarding UX from scratch — reuse/port legitimate UX from the legacy wizard where it doesn't fabricate data.
acceptanceCriteria: No code path computes a readiness/completion percentage from string length or arbitrary formula.
No template evidence is ever persisted to operational_memory without explicit, unedited user authorship being clearly marked as such (or the auto-seed is removed).
The demo-data seeding branch is removed or gated behind an explicit, clearly-labeled 'sample data' affordance never reachable in the default new-user path.
Guardrail test coverage extends to whichever file is the new canonical onboarding entry point.
requiredTests: Extend tests/workspace-onboarding-guardrails.test.mjs to cover the retired/replacement surface
New test asserting a fresh account's operational_memory contains zero rows until the user submits real evidence

backlog.implementationBoundary: Remove the precondition gate in getting-started-flow.tsx; this is likely resolved as a byproduct of PMF-001 if the file is retired, but must be independently verified if the file is instead patched rather than replaced.

acceptanceCriteria: Create Project is reachable and functional for a brand-new workspace with no PMO/Command Center in existence.
No UI copy implies a Command Center is a precondition for Project creation.

backlog.title: Execution-task/dependency mutation endpoints authorize on 'read' not 'write'
evidence: src/lib/security/rbac.ts (executive_viewer/external_stakeholder permission set is {read[, view_executive]} only)
src/app/api/execution-tasks/[taskId]/route.ts:117-124 (newer route correctly gates on "write"; comment confirms legacy route intentionally left at "read" for backward compatibility)
backlog.currentBehavior: A user with a view-only workspace role (executive_viewer, external_stakeholder) can reassign task ownership, change status/due-date/progress, and create/materialize task dependencies through the legacy execution-tasks/update and execution-task-dependencies endpoints, because those routes check for "read" permission instead of "write".
backlog.expectedBehavior: All mutating task/dependency endpoints require "write" permission server-side, consistently with the newer /api/execution-tasks/[taskId] route.
backlog.rootCauseHypothesis: The legacy /update routes predate a later permission-tightening pass that only touched the new [taskId] route; the backward-compatibility comment confirms this was a deliberate but unresolved deferral, not an oversight.
backlog.implementationBoundary: Change the permission argument from "read" to "write" in the four cited call sites; verify no legitimate read-only caller currently depends on the loose gate (check any UI code path that calls these routes for view-only users).
nonGoals: Do not redesign the RBAC permission model itself — this is a call-site fix, not a rbac.ts change.
Do not add tenant-scoping to RLS policies — this is an app-layer authorization fix; RLS already enforces workspace membership.
acceptanceCriteria: An executive_viewer or external_stakeholder session receives a 403 when calling any of the four cited routes with a mutating intent.
Existing legitimate write-role usage of these routes continues to succeed.
requiredTests: New authorization-boundary test: executive_viewer POST to /api/execution-tasks/update returns 403
New authorization-boundary test: external_stakeholder POST to /api/execution-task-dependencies returns 403

backlog.title: pmos table lacks unique constraint on workspace_id — duplicate-PMO race condition
evidence: supabase/migrations/20260527091000_workspace_governance.sql:7 (contrast: workspace_governance has a real PK on workspace_id, race-safe)
src/components/pmfreak/pmo/create-pmo-wizard.tsx:720,810-811 (client-side inFlightRef only guards a single tab/instance)
tests/command-center-activation-sequence.test.mjs:150-152 (only asserts the single-tab guard, no cross-tab/concurrency test)
backlog.currentBehavior: Two concurrent Command Center activation requests for the same workspace (two browser tabs, or a stale retry racing the original request) can both read 'no existing PMO' and both insert, producing two pmos rows for one workspace with no database-level guard against it.
backlog.expectedBehavior: PMO creation is idempotent at the database level — concurrent activation attempts for the same workspace cannot produce duplicate PMO records.
backlog.rootCauseHypothesis: workspace_governance was given a race-safe upsert (PK + onConflict) when the hierarchy migration was written, but the corresponding constraint was never added to pmos, so its check-then-insert path in save-pmo-tenant.ts remains vulnerable.
backlog.implementationBoundary: Add a unique constraint (or partial unique index) on pmos.workspace_id — exact cardinality model depends on the product decision in the audit's Unknowns section (one-PMO-per-workspace vs. multi-PMO with a different idempotency key) — then change save-pmo-tenant.ts to upsert against that constraint instead of check-then-insert.
nonGoals: Do not change the workspace_governance upsert pattern — it is already correct.
Do not solve the client-side silent-retry-no-op bug here (PMF-009) — that is a separate UX defect.
dependencies: Product decision: PMO-per-workspace cardinality (see audit §22 item 5)
acceptanceCriteria: A concurrency test firing two simultaneous activation requests for one workspace results in exactly one pmos row.
Existing single-request activation continues to succeed unchanged.
requiredTests: New concurrency test: two parallel savePmoTenant calls for the same workspace produce one pmos row

backlog.title: 'Project Brain Online'/'smarter' claim renders at zero-evidence state

backlog.expectedBehavior: Any 'Online'/'learning' claim is either removed, or gated on and worded to match what the underlying implementation actually does (a fixed rule-based derivation over onboarding fields and evidence counts, not an adaptive learning system).

backlog.implementationBoundary: Rewrite the hero and operational-memory-panel status copy to accurately describe current capability (e.g., 'Project Brain is tracking N facts from your evidence' rather than 'smarter' framing); gate any 'Online' framing on there being at least one real, non-default statement.
nonGoals: Do not implement actual adaptive learning/confidence scoring here — that is PMF-015's scope, if pursued at all.
Do not remove the Project Brain feature — only its overclaiming copy.

A brand-new project's first Command Center visit shows copy consistent with zero evidence having been provided yet.
requiredTests: New test extending tests/honest-ai-copy.test.mjs (or project-brain-foundation.test.mjs) asserting no 'smarter'/'learns'/'adapts' language is rendered without qualifying evidence

backlog.title: Static onboarding_completed JWT flag diverges from DB-derived activation state
evidence: src/proxy.ts:67-69 (Edge middleware gates on this JWT claim)
src/app/api/onboarding/route.ts:51 and src/app/api/getting-started/route.ts:62 (both write the flag directly)
src/app/(protected)/layout.tsx (calls the DB-backed resolveOnboardingState correctly, but only after the Edge gate has already acted on the stale claim)
backlog.currentBehavior: Edge middleware gating relies on a JWT claim that only refreshes when the session token itself refreshes; a long-lived tab or a workspace state change can leave the gate acting on stale data even though server components elsewhere correctly re-derive live state from the database.
backlog.expectedBehavior: Activation gating is derived from the same live, DB-backed evidence everywhere, including at the Edge middleware layer, or the middleware layer accepts a bounded staleness window explicitly and documents it.
backlog.rootCauseHypothesis: Edge middleware cannot cheaply query the database per-request, so a JWT claim was used as a shortcut; this was never reconciled with the correct, newer DB-derived resolution used in (protected)/layout.tsx.
backlog.implementationBoundary: Either move the Edge gate to a lightweight DB-backed check, or remove enforcement at the Edge layer and rely solely on the DB-backed layout-level check (already present) as the sole authority.
nonGoals: Do not change the evidence-derivation rules themselves (activation-rules.ts).
acceptanceCriteria: A workspace's activation state change (e.g., a project is deleted, invalidating readiness) is reflected in gating decisions within one request, not only after a token refresh.
requiredTests: New test simulating a stale JWT claim against a changed DB state, asserting the DB-backed state wins

backlog.title: Workspace bootstrap is not atomic (orphaned-workspace risk)
evidence: src/lib/workspaces.ts:77-106 (ensureUserWorkspace: two sequential unwrapped writes — workspaces.insert at 92-96, then a separate ensureWorkspaceMembership upsert at 103)
backlog.currentBehavior: New-workspace bootstrap performs a workspace insert and a membership upsert as two separate, non-transactional writes; a process failure between them leaves an orphaned workspace row with no owner membership.
backlog.expectedBehavior: Bootstrap is atomic — either both writes succeed or neither does — via a single transaction or a Postgres function performing both steps.
backlog.rootCauseHypothesis: The two operations were implemented as sequential application-layer calls without wrapping them in a transaction, likely because Supabase's client-side API makes multi-statement transactions less ergonomic than a single insert.
backlog.implementationBoundary: Wrap both writes in a single database transaction (e.g., a Postgres function invoked via RPC) or add a reconciliation check that detects and repairs orphaned workspaces on next login.
nonGoals: Do not change the workspace schema itself.
acceptanceCriteria: A simulated failure between the two writes either rolls back cleanly or is auto-repaired on the user's next request.
requiredTests: New test simulating a membership-upsert failure after a successful workspace insert, asserting no orphaned state is user-visible

backlog.title: Due-date value drifts by a calendar day across creation/display/edit
evidence: src/components/pmfreak/execution/task-due-date-control.tsx:3-11 (toDateInputValue pre-fills the wrong day for negative-UTC-offset viewers)
src/components/pmfreak/execution/task-due-date-control.tsx:45 (onChange writes back using local midnight, inconsistent with the UTC-midnight interpretation used at creation)
backlog.currentBehavior: A due date created via Quick Add (stored as UTC midnight) can display as the previous day, and re-saving it after opening the editor in a timezone behind UTC can silently shift it again, because display and edit round-trip through local time inconsistently with how creation stores the value.
backlog.expectedBehavior: A date-only due date always displays and edits as the same calendar day it was set to, regardless of the viewer's browser timezone.
backlog.rootCauseHypothesis: The due-date field is stored as a full timestamp (UTC midnight) but treated as a date-only value everywhere else; display/edit code paths independently reimplemented local-time conversions instead of sharing one date-only-safe utility.
backlog.implementationBoundary: Introduce a single shared date-only formatting/parsing utility (or store the field as a true date-only Postgres type) and use it consistently across project-task-list.tsx, task-due-date-control.tsx, and any other due-date rendering/editing site.
nonGoals: Do not change timestamp fields that are genuinely instant-in-time (e.g., created_at, uploaded_at) — this applies only to date-only fields like due_date.
acceptanceCriteria: A due date set to a given calendar day displays as that same day for viewers in any timezone.
Opening and re-saving a task's due date without changing it does not alter the stored value.
requiredTests: New test asserting due-date round-trip stability across simulated timezones (e.g., UTC-12 through UTC+14)

backlog.title: Command Center activation retry silently no-ops after client timeout
evidence: src/components/pmfreak/pmo/create-pmo-wizard.tsx:868-871 (inFlightRef cleared only in the original request's finally)
src/components/pmfreak/pmo/create-pmo-wizard.tsx:880-882 (handleRetryActivation -> handleCreate hits the guard, silently no-ops)
src/lib/pmo/save-pmo-tenant.ts:128-149 (the underlying non-idempotent call this retry races against)
backlog.currentBehavior: If the client's 20-second submit timeout fires while the original activation request is still pending server-side, clicking Retry hits the in-flight guard and does nothing visible — no spinner, no error, no feedback — until the stale request eventually settles.
backlog.expectedBehavior: Retry either genuinely retries (once the original request is confirmed dead) or gives the user clear, honest feedback that a previous attempt is still being processed.
backlog.rootCauseHypothesis: The in-flight guard was designed to prevent duplicate submissions within a single request lifecycle but doesn't account for the client-side timeout firing before the guard clears, leaving a window where Retry is a no-op.
backlog.implementationBoundary: Either surface a 'still processing your previous request' state when the guard is active during a retry attempt, or resolve PMF-004's idempotency fix first so a genuine retry is always safe to fire immediately.
nonGoals: Do not change the 20-second timeout value itself — this is a feedback/behavior fix, not a tuning change.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking Retry while the original request is still in flight shows a visible 'still working' state rather than doing nothing.
requiredTests: New test simulating a slow original request and asserting Retry gives visible feedback rather than a silent no-op

nonGoals: Do not add real backend initialization work purely to justify the existing copy — fix the copy to match reality, or remove the staged reveal.

backlog.title: Project Brain episode/knowledge timestamps use project-creation time, not real event time
evidence: src/components/pmfreak/intelligence-inbox/project-intelligence-inbox.tsx:246 (generatedAt fixed to project.createdAt for every statement)
src/lib/project-brain/derive-initial-response.ts:256-264 (a FACT about N evidence items is stamped with the project's creation date even if those items were uploaded weeks later)
backlog.currentBehavior: Every knowledge/gap/question episode in the timeline is stamped with the project's creation timestamp rather than the timestamp of the evidence or event that actually produced the underlying fact, so the timeline clusters all such episodes on day one regardless of when they were actually learned.
backlog.expectedBehavior: Each derived statement/episode carries the timestamp of the real evidence or event that produced it, not a single fixed value shared across all statements.
backlog.rootCauseHypothesis: buildInitialProjectBrainResponse was implemented to take one generatedAt value for the whole response rather than per-statement, likely because the initial rule-based derivation didn't yet need per-statement granularity.
backlog.implementationBoundary: Thread the originating evidence/event's real timestamp through to each individual statement and episode, rather than one shared generatedAt value at the response level.
nonGoals: Do not change episode persistence model (still virtual/derived per PMF design) — this is a timestamp-accuracy fix, not a persistence architecture change.
acceptanceCriteria: A fact derived from evidence uploaded on day 10 of a project shows a day-10 timestamp in the episode timeline, not day 1.
requiredTests: New test asserting statement/episode timestamps match their originating evidence row's timestamp, not the project's createdAt

backlog.title: Evidence/context timeline silently caps at 20 rows with no pagination
evidence: src/lib/operational-flow/operational-flow-service.ts:85 (.order("created_at",{ascending:false}).limit(20), no pagination anywhere in the UI)

backlog.title: Project Brain confidence levels are hardcoded per statement type, not computed
evidence: src/lib/project-brain/types.ts:68-76 (a "scored" confidence variant with score/method/scoredBy exists)
src/lib/project-brain/derive-initial-response.ts:107,127,147,160,178 (fixed constant per epistemic type: FACT→high, REPORTED→medium, OPEN_QUESTION→low, UNKNOWN→unknown, RECOMMENDATION→low)

requiredTests: New test asserting confidence-related UI copy matches the actual derivation method used

backlog.title: Audit-event write failures are unchecked and unlogged

nonGoals: Do not make audit-event failures block or roll back the primary mutation.
